passages.paragraph_text: Once you have to spend $4,000 to get on an airplane and go fix the problem, that gets costly. But, you know, there are times when it's useful. Like, so I've designed – for the past five years, I've designed the electronic badge for DEF CON, which is a hacker conference in Las Vegas. And the world's largest – That's pretty cool. Yeah, you know, around 8,000 to 10,000 people go. And so on my website, there's links to the actual products. But those were – you know, we had to make 8,000 of those. And cost was very, very – we had to keep cost down. And, you know, Jeff Moss, the founder of the conference, was like, well, can you do something for $5? I'm like, complete, you know, assembled and parts and everything. And that's where we started. It was a $5 bomb. So the most recent one for DEF CON 18, and I stopped doing it after five years, but DEF CON 18 was, I think, $14 because we had an aluminum substrate board with laser engraving and all sorts of crazy stuff. But to get that many done, I ended up – I was using a facility in China called e-teknet, E-T-E-K-N-E-T, who I'd done a lot of volume work with before. And, you know, their quality was good, but I still had to stay on them. You know, it was almost daily updates making sure that they were, you know, incorporating the changes that had to be done. And then, you know, they were able to pull it off. And, you know, they ended up – for a few of the years, they ended up having to manufacture all 8,000 boards within three days. And they pulled it off. You know, and it was – so they're definitely – you know, it depends on the project. There's times to be local. There's times to go offshore. You know, if it's quality, if it's price, if it's, you know, delivery speed. Then you have to deal with customs. So there's all these things that you have to consider. It's not just let's go to China.
